title: Data Center Engineering Operations - 2027 Internship
description:
Want to be part of the team that keeps the world's largest cloud running? As an Engineering Operations Technician Intern at Amazon Web Services (AWS), you will get hands-on experience with the critical infrastructure behind Amazon's global data centers — and your work will directly impact millions of customers worldwide.

This internship is designed as a potential pathway to full-time employment. Interns who demonstrate strong performance throughout their internship may be considered for a full-time Engineering Operations Technician position, subject to available roles and business needs.

Who Should Apply

We welcome applications from:

Students in the last year of their Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field who are looking for an internship that could lead to a full-time career.



About the Role

As an intern, you will provide technical support within Amazon's owned and operated data centers. Your work will ensure that the data center's mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems operate at 100% availability while maintaining first-class customer service to the teams and groups on site.

You will be exposed to both independent work and team-based collaboration. Prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to being successful.

What You Will Do

The Engineering Operations team is Amazon's front-line responders for hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations. You will work with equipment that supports mission-critical servers and must maintain better than 99.999% uptime. This equipment includes, but is not limited to:

- Stand-by diesel generators and switchgear

- Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPSs) and Power Distribution Units (PDUs)

- Air Handling Units (AHUs), chillers, and cooling towers

- Chemical treatment systems, pumps, motors, and Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs)

- Building automation systems

Your day-to-day duties include:

- Maintaining mechanical and electrical equipment

- Assisting with root cause analysis of equipment failures

- Troubleshooting facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLAs)

- Taking daily operational readings of all mechanical and electrical equipment

- Using internal Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS) to manage building workflows

- Interacting with third-party vendors and contractors working on site

Internship Structure

Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for 12 consecutive weeks. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Monday through Friday.

Please note that full-time Engineering Operations Technician roles operate on a rotating shift pattern, which may include days, nights, weekends, and public holidays. Candidates should be willing and able to commit to shift work upon transitioning to a full-time position.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed below, we encourage you to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let that stop you from applying.

Your Career at Amazon — A Universe of Opportunity

At Amazon, your career is not a straight path. It is a journey you build as you go.

From your first day as an intern, you will own real work that matters. You will troubleshoot and maintain the systems that keep AWS running for millions of customers. Your mentors and teammates will champion your growth, helping you build skills you did not know existed — and you will see your work come to life at massive scale.

Impact. Your work shapes the infrastructure that millions of customers rely on every day. From cloud computing to artificial intelligence, the systems you maintain power it all.

Action. You will move fast, experiment, and learn by doing. Your ideas do not get stuck in approval chains — they get tested, refined, and put into practice.

Curiosity. Every project teaches you something new. You will apply what you learned in the classroom to real challenges and explore different teams, technologies, and career paths within Amazon.

Mentorship and career growth. You will start with structured onboarding and get paired with experienced mentors. Beyond that, you will find continuous learning opportunities and the chance to work on different projects. Your journey here is yours to shape.

A day in the life

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on.

You will join a diverse team of engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers.

title: Simulation Engineer - Drone Physical Models Integration
description:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As our GNC, ML, Embedded Software, and Validation teams scale, they rely increasingly on simulation to develop and test our autonomous defense systems. The value of that simulation depends directly on how faithfully it reproduces the real behavior of our drones.

Joining the Tooling team, you will be responsible for bringing the physical models of our drones into the simulator—including aerodynamics, propulsion, electronics, sensors, and electromechanical systems. Designed by expert domain teams, these models require your expertise to translate user needs, integrate models into the simulator software stack, and validate expected behavior. Because not every use case requires the same level of realism, you will help establish the appropriate fidelity targets across applications.

This role offers high ownership and the opportunity to work at the intersection of physics, software engineering, and AI robotics with direct mission impact.

Responsibilities

  • Coordination with Domain Experts: Work with the teams in charge of aerodynamics, propulsion, electronics, sensors, and electromechanical systems to understand their models, their assumptions, and their inputs and outputs, and to agree on how they are delivered to the simulator.

  • Model Integration: Integrate these models into the simulator software stack in a clean, performant, and maintainable way, with clear interfaces and configurable parameters.

  • Validation: Define and run tests that check the integrated models against the reference data given by the expert teams (flight logs, bench tests, manufacturer data), and report discrepancies back to the model owners.

  • User Needs & Fidelity Targets: Work with the simulator users (GNC, Embedded, Validation) to understand their use cases, and translate them into a realism target for each model. Pick the right balance between fidelity, performance, and integration effort, and prioritise the model integration work to match.

  • Documentation & Standards: Document the integrated models, their parameters, validity domains, and validation results, and help standardise the model integration and validation process.

Candidate requirements

  • Experience: Minimum of 3 years of professional experience in software engineering, simulation, or a related engineering field.

  • Physics Understanding: Good understanding of flight dynamics and enough physics background to discuss models with experts in aerodynamics, propulsion, electronics, sensors, and electromechanical systems, and to turn their models into working code.

  • Integration & Validation: Experience integrating third-party models or components into a larger software system, and validating them against experimental data with a rigorous approach.

  • Technical Proficiency: Comfortable with C++ and Python, with a good knowledge of Linux environments.

  • Educational Background: MSc or BSc in Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Applied Physics, or a similar technical field; equivalent professional experience is equally valued.

Plus (nice to have)

  • Experience with drones or robotic systems, ideally with open-source autopilots like PX4 or ArduPilot.

  • Hands-on experience with flight testing, test benches, or log analysis.

  • French language skills.

Mindset

  • Rigor: Empirical and disciplined about validation, grounded in real test data, and skeptical of a result that only exists in simulation.

  • Communication: Clear written and verbal communication, comfortable working with several specialized teams, asking the right questions, and sharing validation results with them.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Data Center Operation Technician
description:
G'day! You've found an opportunity that could define your next chapter.

Applicants must be Australian citizens and hold or be eligible to obtain an Australian Government Security Clearance with the ability to successfully complete an Organisational Suitability Assessment. More information regarding security clearances can be found at https://www.agsva.gov.au/.

The Mission — Why This Programme, Why Now?
You're joining at the defining moment of one of the most significant technology programmes Australia has ever undertaken. This programme will build and operate the dedicated cloud giving Australia's national security community and its allies the capability to see more, share more, innovate and act faster than ever before.

The architectural decisions being made now — how we structure networking, implement security controls, and automate at scale — will shape how Australia's national security community operates for the next decade.

Your Role in the Story
Imagine being the person who keeps one of the world's largest and most critical information system infrastructures running at peak performance. As a Data Centre Technician, you'll be the hands-on expert who ensures the physical backbone of the cloud never misses a beat. Every server you deploy, every cable you run, every issue you troubleshoot directly enables Australia's national security community to operate with confidence.

This isn't just maintenance — it's mission-critical stewardship. You'll apply deep knowledge of computer architecture and the OSI model to solve complex, real-world problems that most engineers only read about. Your troubleshooting instincts will span server hardware, fibre optics, networking, and beyond. When something goes wrong at 2am, you'll be the calm, capable expert the team relies on.

Benefits

- Learning & development — AWS training and certification support, access to internal learning platforms.
- Health, income protection and life cover — Amazon subsidises private health insurance premiums, and group salary continuance and life insurance are included at no cost to you.
- Military differential pay launching in Australia — Australian employees taking defence reserve leave may receive up to 52 weeks of military differential pay to help cover the difference in pay while serving.
- Employee Assistance Program — Free, confidential support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for you and your family — mental health, financial coaching, legal questions, and everyday life events.
- Family-building benefit — Access to Maven for fertility treatment, adoption support, surrogacy, and parenting coaching.
- Amazon Extras & employee discount — cashback and discounts across hundreds of retail, fitness, travel, and lifestyle partners.

Key job responsibilities
You'll own the full lifecycle of physical data centre infrastructure — from the moment new capacity is planned to the day legacy equipment is gracefully retired. Your days will blend strategic thinking with hands-on execution in ways that keep you constantly engaged.

Building and Deploying

You'll install and configure racks to internal SLAs, plan and track capacity, and deploy cabling infrastructure that forms the nervous system of the cloud. Every rack you stand up expands Australia's sovereign capability.

Troubleshooting and Resolving

When trouble tickets land, you'll prioritise with precision and resolve with speed. You'll serve as the escalation point for all systems issues — the person teams turn to when problems get complex. Your Linux expertise will be your superpower as you deep dive into server-level challenges that others can't crack.

Leading Through Complexity

During high-severity incidents, you'll be the technical point of contact — coordinating response, communicating clearly, and driving resolution. You'll meet 24x7 on-call requirements during shift rotations, knowing that your vigilance directly protects national capability.

Physical Excellence

You'll work confidently with equipment up to 20 kg, navigate cramped spaces and elevated locations, and do it all within rigorous health and safety guidelines. This is infrastructure work at its most tangible and rewarding.

title: Lead RF Engineer - Electronic Warfare
description:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As an Lead RF Engineer - Electronic Warfare, you will own the delivery of our electronic warfare and signal intelligence systems - from concept to field deployment. You will work hand-in-hand with project managers and technical leads to translate mission needs into system-level designs, coordinate multidisciplinary engineering teams, and ensure overall system performance, robustness, and reliability. The capability to detect, investigate, and exploit system vulnerabilities.

Responsibilities

  • Electronic Warfare Team: Build, maintain and manage a cross disciplinary Electronic Warfare Engineering Team.

  • Electronic Warfare Systems and Technology watch: Drive architecture and implementation of Electronic Warfare Systems. Ensure state of the art knowledge in EW/SIGINT.

  • Technical Coordination: Lead cross-functional design across mechanical, electrical, software, GNC, and ML teams.

  • Trade-Off & Design Analysis: Conduct feasibility studies, trade-off analyses, and system-level simulations to guide technical choices.

  • Integration & Validation: Oversee system integration, prototyping, and validation, ensuring performance targets are achieved.

  • System Reviews: Drive design and architecture reviews, maintaining consistency between requirements, design, and testing.

  • Continuous Improvement: Implement processes to enhance requirements traceability, system documentation, and validation workflows.

Candidate Requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in RF system engineering of Radio/Radar/GNSS and other Sensors within robotics, aerospace, or defense sectors.

  • Experience in Technology leadership in EW/SIGINT is a strong plus

  • Experience in Team leadership is a bonus, but not required

  • MSc in Engineering; PhD is a plus.

  • Proven experience leading full system lifecycles (concept → prototype → validation).

  • Strong background in RF, GNSS and Radar system architecture, requirements engineering, and system level trade-off analysis.

  • RF Signal Intelligence gathering and analysis for classification and AI training.

  • Broad engineering culture with understanding of mechanical, electrical, and embedded systems.

  • Experience coordinating multi-disciplinary teams and managing technical interfaces.

  • Rigorous, structured, and mission-driven mindset with strong analytical skills.

  • Excellent communication and documentation abilities.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

title: Senior AI Transformation Consultant
description:
Who We Are

Build. Scale. Sustain.

We are a global technology consultancy with a trademarked, AI-first engineering approach for accelerating the delivery of digital products, and revolutionizing platform modernization. We do the right thing, and we do it right. We're proud to be a World Economic Forum New Champion, and a B Corp-certified company.

  • We are small enough to care locally, big enough to deliver globally: 5 continents, 10 countries, +500 experts from +50 nationalities across the Americas, Europe and APAC

  • We are robust and resilient: 100% independent and 0 debt

  • We are entrepreneurs and passionate experts: We invest in what we believe genuinely and work as a collective intelligence

  • We are positive, courageous, caring, doers and committed to excellence

About Gen-e2TM
While the market is still largely AI-augmenting delivery, we have reinvented the SDLC to be AI First. Leveraging our 16 years expertise in digital transformation, our approach is a game-changer in productivity and quality, with a strong collaboration between IA generative and our best Talents:

  • We now generate 95% of the entire product — code, documentation, infrastructure as code, and even design powered by GitHub Copilot.

  • The quality consistently exceeds the output of our best traditional engineering teams.

  • A product repository houses all product artefacts, giving AI full project context for higher-quality generation.

  • A library of rules and prompts defines coding standards, design principles, and security guidelines, ensuring enterprise-grade quality and scalability.

With Gen-e2TM, we deliver end-to-end products 2–3× faster than traditional approaches, while raising the bar for engineering excellence.

YOUR ROLE

PALO IT is an AI-enabled software delivery consultancy helping enterprises transform how they build products and run programs. Our Gen-e2 methodology sits at the heart of this work — a structured approach to embedding AI augmentation across the full software delivery lifecycle, from discovery to deployment.

We're looking for a Senior AI Transformation Consultant to join the Gen-e2 Pilots & Transformation team. This role centres on helping clients turn AI ambition into lasting organisational change. You will shape transformation roadmaps, align stakeholders, guide teams through new ways of working, and ensure that AI initiatives deliver measurable business value. If you enjoy navigating complexity, building momentum across organisations, and helping people adopt meaningful change, this role is for you.

Key Responsibilities

Transformation Program Delivery

  • Lead or co-lead AI pilot and transformation programs end-to-end: scoping, delivery, measurement, iterating and pivoting

  • Work embedded in client delivery teams, coaching engineers, product owners, business analysts and delivery leads on AI-augmented product discovery and delivery practices

  • Identify and track meaningful metrics — productivity uplift, backlog quality, cycle time — to demonstrate and sustain value for the client

  • Lead the discovery work that opens an engagement: assess the client's current SDLC and constraints, appetite for change and select real use cases from their backlog

  • Design and facilitate the development of transformation roadmaps for clients, sequencing capability building, tooling adoption, and organisational change across waves

  • Support the setup and operationalisation of client AI Centre of Excellence (CoE): governance models, ways of working, role definitions, and capability frameworks

  • Collaborate with PALO IT practice leads to evolve the methodology based on field learnings

AI Engineering

  • Co-Design and build AI toolchains with our Gen-e2 Engineers — agentic workflows, MCP integrations, AI-assisted SDLC pipelines — deployed in real client environments

  • Architect multi-agent systems and automation across the delivery lifecycle (backlog refinement, code generation, test automation, impact analysis)

  • Evaluate and integrate emerging AI tooling (models, frameworks, IDEs, orchestration layers) into structured delivery patterns

Pre-sales & Business Development

  • Participate in client discovery and proposal work, contributing technical credibility and realistic scoping

  • Help shape AI capability assessments, pilot proposals, and transformation roadmaps

Thought Leadership

  • Write articles, case studies, or technical posts that articulate PALO IT's point of view on AI-augmented delivery and the Gen-e2 methodology

  • Speak at industry events, conferences, and client forums — representing both technical depth and transformation experience

  • Contribute to PALO IT's external presence on LinkedIn and other channels, sharing learnings from the field

  • Help develop frameworks, whitepapers, or playbooks that advance the practice internally and build credibility externally

What We're Looking For

Must-haves

  • Familiarity with the modern AI tooling ecosystem (coding assistants, MCP servers, agent frameworks)

  • Hands-on experience with AI-augmented SDLC

  • Stakeholder management

  • Facilitation and training

  • Change management / transformation (roadmapping, KPIs...)

  • Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders

  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-moving client environments

  • Working knowledge of Agile, Lean, and Systems Thinking principles

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience in agile/software delivery consulting or a similar advisory context

  • Exposure to pre-sales, RFP responses, or client proposal work

  • Background in financial services, government, or regulated industries

  • Familiarity with Agile frameworks and practices

Mindset

  • Growth mindset — you see every engagement, setback, and experiment as an opportunity to learn and improve, both for yourself and the teams around you

  • Leading by example — you don't just advise; you roll up your sleeves, demonstrate, and set the standard through your own work

  • Strong accountability — you take ownership of outcomes, not just activities; you follow through, flag issues early, and hold yourself to a high bar

  • Willingness to experiment — in a field moving as fast as AI, you're energised by uncertainty; you test, iterate, and share what you learn openly

More About PALO IT

We’re eager to adapt to change, learn from our experiences and move to meet our planet’s urgent needs. We are continuously taking action to:

  • Become a climate net-zero company

  • Deliver projects with a positive impact

  • Train 100% of our workforce on impact

  • Achieve B Corp certification among all our offices across the globe

  • Continuously measure & improve employee happiness

Our clients are amongst the world's most successful companies. We innovate with both established Fortune 1000s, SMEs and start-ups who aim to make an impact, become global leaders and address the world's most complex challenges.

What We Offer

  • Stimulating working environments

  • Unique career path

  • International mobility

  • Internal R&D projects

  • Knowledge sharing

  • Personalized training

  • Entrepreneurship & intrapreneurship

For more on our team culture and benefits, check out our careers page.

title: Receptioniste Lage Weide/Rivium, Rotterdam
description:
Ben jij gastvrij, betrokken en vind je het leuk om ervoor te zorgen dat iedereen zich welkom voelt? Voor onze locatie Lage Weide zijn wij op zoek naar een enthousiaste gastheer/gastvrouw.

Lage Weide is een kinderdagcentrum waar kinderen gedurende de dag begeleiding, ondersteuning en een fijne plek krijgen om zichzelf te ontwikkelen. Als gastheer/gastvrouw ben jij een vertrouwd gezicht en een belangrijk aanspreekpunt voor kinderen, ouders, bezoekers en collega’s.

Met jouw gastvrije houding, organisatietalent en betrokkenheid zorg je ervoor dat de locatie prettig en toegankelijk aanvoelt. Je houdt het overzicht, helpt waar nodig en draagt eraan bij dat de dagelijkse gang van zaken soepel verloopt. Een veelzijdige rol waarin jouw aanwezigheid écht het verschil maakt.

Wat ga je doen?

Als gastheer/gastvrouw ben je het eerste aanspreekpunt op locatie Lage Weide. Je ontvangt bezoekers en beantwoordt de telefoon. Daarnaast verricht je verschillende lichte administratieve werkzaamheden en verzorg je de inkomende en uitgaande post.

Ook heb je een belangrijke rol in de ontvangst van de kinderen die naar de dagbesteding komen. Je vangt hen op en begeleidt hen, wanneer dat nodig is, naar de juiste dagbesteding.

Je werkzaamheden zijn afwisselend en vragen om een gastvrije, servicegerichte en zorgvuldige houding.

Bijzonderheden:

  • je vaste werkdag is vrijdag;

  • bij afwezigheid van collega’s kun je, indien nodig, worden ingezet op andere locaties.

Wie ben jij?

Je bent gastvrij, zorgvuldig en vindt het leuk om met verschillende mensen contact te hebben. Je kunt goed zelfstandig werken, maar zoekt ook graag de samenwerking met collega’s. Daarnaast heb je affiniteit met kinderen en onze doelgroep.

Verder:

  • heb je een afgeronde opleiding op mbo-niveau 2;

  • werk je nauwkeurig en accuraat;

  • ben je servicegericht en flexibel;

  • kun je zowel zelfstandig als in teamverband werken;

  • heb je affiniteit met de doelgroep;

  • beheers je de Nederlandse taal goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk;

  • heb je ervaring met of kennis van Microsoft Office, waaronder Word en Excel.

Wat bieden wij?
ASVZ wil niet alleen een goede zorgverlener zijn, maar ook een goede werkgever. Een organisatie waar je met plezier werkt en waar je je verbonden voelt met je collega’s.

Verder kun je rekenen op:

  • een dienstverband van minimaal 9 uur per week;

  • een jaarcontract met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband;

  • volop ruimte voor ontwikkeling;

  • een salaris volgens FWG 30 (max. € 3.385,00 bruto per maand o.b.v. 36 uur);

  • 8% vakantietoeslag en 8,33% eindejaarsuitkering.

Enthousiast?

Zie jij jezelf in deze rol bij ASVZ? Dan kijken we uit naar je sollicitatie. Eerst sparren over de functie? Bel of app gerust met Gerda de Jong, Teamleider Recepties, Portiers en Bewaking via 0184-491200.

title: Senior Product Designer, Learner App (m/f/d)
description:
We're building a new global Berlitz, and this is your opportunity to help shape it. Nearly 150 years of expertise, meeting the ambition and technology to power a new era of learning.

If you are the kind of person who thrives in a fast-paced environment, isn’t afraid of a blank page, and is excited to help shape the future of a global company undergoing a significant transformation, you might belong at Berlitz!

Berlitz has taught languages for almost 150 years, mostly in classrooms and with live teachers. Now we're putting that method in people's pockets. The Berlitz app connects structured lessons, AI speaking and writing practice, 1:1 sessions with human tutors, and visible progress into one learning loop on iOS and Android. We're launching it market by market, and growing it fast.

Our learners are professionals who need a language for their career. Some pay for themselves. Others get Berlitz through their employer, who wants proof the investment is working. Both need an app they open every day because it helps them, and keep paying for because they can see themselves getting better.

As Senior Product Designer, you'll own major parts of the learner app, from the first minute after download to the moment someone books their tenth tutor session. You'll report to the Staff Product Designer for this area of the business, and partner as an equal with Product Management, Engineering, and our AI and learning experience teams.

What you'll be doing

  • Design core learner journeys end to end across iOS and Android: onboarding and placement, daily learning, AI practice, tutor booking, progress, and the path from free to paid.

  • Design for habit and momentum. Find out why learners come back, why they drop off, and what makes them feel progress, then build that into the product.

  • Shape how learners speak and write with AI: conversational interfaces, real-time feedback on pronunciation and writing, and the moments where an AI tutor should hand over to a human one.

  • Work AI-native every day. Use AI design tools and agentic workflows to explore, prototype, and produce at speed, while staying the human in the loop who decides what's good enough to ship.

  • Pressure-test every PRD before it becomes a design. Question the assumptions, find the missing edge cases, and sharpen the problem with your PM, instead of passing a brief straight to a tool and accepting what comes back.

  • Hold AI output to a high bar. Run rigorous evals on what AI produces for craft, accessibility, localisation, and brand fit. When you see the same problem twice, fix it at the source by updating the design system.

  • Run research yourself. Talk to learners often, run usability tests, read the analytics, and set up experiments that tell us whether a change worked.

  • Own the conversion and retention moments (trials, paywalls, upgrade prompts, reminders) so they earn revenue without costing the learner's trust.

  • Design for corporate learners too: employer-paid access, entitlements, and the progress their company expects to see, without making the app feel corporate.

  • Build with Berlitz's shared design system and help it evolve, especially the mobile patterns, motion, and micro-interactions a daily-use app needs. Keep it structured so that both people and AI tools use it correctly.

  • Design for many markets and languages from the start, including text expansion, right-to-left scripts, and accessibility.

  • Work closely with engineers to ship fast, then sweat the details once it's live.

What we're looking for

  • Several years designing and shipping consumer mobile apps that people use every day, with a portfolio that shows native iOS and Android craft.

  • Evidence that your design work moved retention, engagement, or conversion, and a clear view of how you measured it.

  • Strong interaction and visual design. You care how a screen feels in the hand: motion, feedback, and pacing, as well as how it looks.

  • Hands-on research and experimentation. You've run your own interviews and usability tests, and used A/B tests and analytics to make calls.

  • An understanding of B2B: how a product changes when the person paying isn't the person using it, and how to serve both.

  • Real experience with AI design tools (currently we mostly use Claude Design) and agentic workflows. You use tools like Claude Design, Figma Make, or Paper, and AI coding tools like Claude Code daily, and you can show examples where you rejected or reworked an AI output and explain why.

  • Experience working within a design system and extending it.

  • Clear communication, and the confidence to push back on PMs, engineers, and senior stakeholders with reasoning they can act on.

  • Fluent English. Another language is a plus. We are a language company, after all.

  • Based in Germany, Switzerland, or Hungary.

Nice to have

  • A background in a learning, language, or content app, or another product built on a daily habit (reading, audio, fitness).

  • Experience with freemium and subscription models, including app store payment flows.

  • Experience designing for markets in Latin America or South Asia.

  • Experience taking work from AI design tools to code to the repo. That means pushing front-end changes yourself through pull requests and checking your work in iOS and Android simulators.

What we offer

  • A product that changes careers. Our learners need the language for a job, a promotion, or a move abroad. Your work helps them get there.

  • Real ownership, early. Large parts of the learner app are yours to shape while the product is still young.

  • A combination few learning apps have. A recognized learning method, a global network of human teachers, and an AI team building practice and tutoring on top.

  • One global Berlitz. Join a company actively rebuilding itself, with new products, new systems, and new ways of working across every team.

  • Remote-first flexibility, based in Germany, Switzerland, Hungary, or Netherlands.

At Berlitz, connecting people across languages and cultures is at the heart of what we do. Our global workplace reflects the diverse world we serve, bringing together different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We create an inclusive environment where everyone has an equal opportunity to belong, contribute and grow.

Ready to shape what’s next? Join us and help build the future with us.

title: Basispsycholoog eetstoornissen
description:
Ben jij een ervaren basispsycholoog die graag het verschil maakt in de behandeling van cliënten met eetstoornissen? Werk je graag samen in een multidisciplinair team om het verschil te maken in de behandeling van complexe problematiek? Wij zoeken therapeuten die net als wij geloven in een benadering waarin professionele nabijheid, gelijkwaardigheid en zorg vanuit levenservaring centraal staan. Iets voor jou? Lees dan snel verder!

Wij zijn Human Concern, een gespecialiseerde GGZ instelling voor eetstoornissen die evidence based interventies waaronder CGT, schematherapie en EMDR combineert met inzet van je eigen levens-/herstelervaring. Bij Human Concern geloven we in een holistische benadering waarin niet enkel gefocust wordt op de symptomen van de eetstoornis, maar ook veel aandacht is voor de functie van de eetstoornis, de triggers en instandhoudende factoren. We werken met een specifieke groep cliënten die bewust voor onze therapeutische behandelvisie kiezen en daarvoor ook de benodigde motivatie inbrengen.

Onafhankelijk onderzoek toont aan dat werken vanuit gelijkwaardig, wezenlijk contact een bepalende factor kan zijn voor het succesvol behandelen van eetstoornissen. Vanuit de visie van Human Concern werken wij hiervoor met ervaringsprofessionals, dit zijn o.a. GGZ-agogen en basispsychologen die zelf zijn hersteld van een eetstoornis of een vergelijkbaar life changing event en hebben geleerd om deze ervaring professioneel in te zetten tijdens de behandeling. Als basispsycholoog ben jij een belangrijke schakel in het leveren van kwalitatief hoge en effectieve zorg door je inhoudelijke expertise en rol binnen het multidisciplinaire team.

Jij als Ervaringsprofessional binnen ons team

Als basispsycholoog werk je bij Human Concern in de rol van Ervaringsprofessional. Ervaringsprofessionals zijn zorgprofessionals die zelf zijn hersteld van een eetstoornis of een vergelijkbaar life changing event en hebben geleerd om deze ervaring professioneel in te zetten. Je behandelt cliënten voornamelijk individueel en daarnaast in groepsverband. Je organiseert, coördineert en bewaakt de behandelactiviteiten en bent het aanspreekpunt voor cliënten, naastbetrokkenen en andere hulpverleners. Je staat stevig in je schoenen, of nog beter, je hebt geleerd dat werkelijke kracht ligt in kwetsbaarheid, oprechtheid en het erkennen van je eigen menselijkheid en dat van de ander.

Vanuit de visie van Human Concern werk je in een gelijkwaardig multidisciplinair team dat bestaat uit een diëtist, systeemtherapeut, GZ- of klinisch psycholoog, arts en psychiater. Je stelt samen met je cliënten, conform onze zorgpaden, een behandelplan op waarbij de naastbetrokkenen (het systeem) standaard worden betrokken. Je staat naast je collega's en naast de cliënt en durft buiten vastomlijnde kaders te zoeken naar de juiste ingang voor een succesvolle behandeling. Tijdens multidisciplinair overleg denk je actief mee. De GZ- of klinisch psycholoog ondersteunt je in zijn/haar rol van regiebehandelaar en als eindverantwoordelijke van het traject met de uitwerking van het behandelplan en middels werkbegeleiding.

Wat kun jij van ons verwachten?

  • Alle voorwaarden uit de CAO GGZ;

  • Een salaris tussen €4.544,- en €5.901,- per maand;

  • Een werkomgeving binnen een team met enthousiaste en professionele medewerkers;

  • Goede secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden. Collectiviteitskorting bij je ziektekostenverzekering, pensioenopbouw bij Pensioenfonds Zorg en Welzijn, 166 vakantie-uren bij een fulltime dienstverband, 35 uur aan levensfasebudget (LFB) naast je (bovenwettelijke) vakantie-uren bij een fulltime dienstverband, een jaarlijkse 8,33% vakantietoeslag, 8,33% eindejaarsuitkering en tot slot is er een balansbudget. Het balansbudget kan je inzetten voor persoonlijke scholing, vrije dagen of laten uitbetalen.

Wat verwachten wij van jou?
Je bent zelfbewust en weet hoe je de verbinding met de ander kan maken. Je beschikt over een goed gevulde rugzak die je in staat stelt om ook zonder de kaders van vaste protocollen een hoogwaardige behandeling te bieden. Daarnaast vragen wij:

  • Een afgeronde wo (master)opleiding tot basispsycholoog;

  • Je bent in het bezit van een LOGO-verklaring;

  • Beschikbaar voor minimaal 24 uur en maximaal 32 uur per week;

  • De bereidheid om je eigen levenservaring professioneel in te zetten.

Nieuwsgierig?

Wil je kennismaken, sfeer proeven of ontdekken of Human Concern bij je past? Neem dan laagdrempelig contact op met Dennis Bot - d.bot@humanconcern.nl - 06-43160757. We maken graag kennis met je, ook als je oriënterend bent!

  • Design, build, evaluate and deploy automations for agentic workflows, retrieval strategies, and LLM-powered data pipelines.

  • Creating evals for multi-step agent workflows

  • Add proactive intelligence inside the data pipelines from ingestion all the way to consumption

  • Create interfaces that make agent behavior easier to inspect, steer, and trust by internal users

You can also expect to:

  • Take ownership of our codebase, balancing high-quality code, security and speed of development

  • Own and drive forward PoCs and solve broad technical challenges

  • Proven history developing and maintaining production-grade software and systems

Big Plus

Our Offer

  • Opportunity to work and learn in a tech start-up environment

  • To help us make an impact in the race to net zero

  • The excitement and fun of being part of a growing, dedicated and professional start-up

title: Verzorgende IG flexpool
description:
Wat ga je doen?
Als Verzorgende IG in de flexpool werk je op verschillende locaties, afdelingen en met verschillende doelgroepen binnen BrabantZorg. Je helpt daar waar jouw inzet nodig is en draagt bij aan goede zorg voor onze cliënten.

De zorg gaat 24/7 door en de behoefte aan medewerkers verschilt per locatie en moment. Daarom verwachten we van jou dat je flexibel inzetbaar bent. Je werkt niet alleen overdag, maar bent ook beschikbaar voor diensten in de avonden, weekenden en op feestdagen. Daarnaast kan het nodig zijn dat je op verschillende locaties of afdelingen werkt, afhankelijk van waar de zorgbehoefte het grootst is.

Binnen die kaders heb je zelf invloed op je planning. Via ons roostersysteem InPlanning zie je de openstaande diensten en schrijf je jezelf in op beschikbare diensten. Je bent zelf verantwoordelijk voor het plannen van voldoende uren binnen je contract.

Zo is jouw dag ‘Elke dag zo fijn mogelijk’:

  • Je werkt op verschillende afdelingen met verschillende doelgroepen;

  • Je ondersteunt, begeleidt en verzorgt cliënten met ‘echte’ aandacht;

  • Je hebt invloed op je eigen planning;

  • Je draagt bij waar jouw inzet het hardst nodig is.

Voor de flexpool werken we met een contract van 0 tot 28 uur per week.

Soms is er een periodieke hulpvraag. Dit houdt in dat je de mogelijkheid krijgt om een periode-opdracht van minimaal vier weken tot maximaal zes maanden uit te voeren op één afdeling en/of locatie. Dit gaat altijd in overleg.

Wat krijg je van ons?

  • Een contract van 0 tot 28 uur per week, waarbij je zelf invloed hebt op het plannen van je uren;

  • Een salaris volgens FWG 35 van de cao VVT;

  • Een eindejaarsuitkering van 8,3% (een volledige dertiende maand), 8% vakantiegeld en een goede pensioenregeling;

  • Collectieve verzekeringen en meerkeuze in arbeidsvoorwaarden met fiscaal voordeel, zoals een laptop- of fietsregeling;

  • Een uitgebreide keuze aan trainingen en opleidingen via de BrabantZorg Academie om jezelf te blijven ontwikkelen.

Wie ben jij?

Allereerst heb jij hart voor de ouderenzorg. Jij hebt een diploma tot Verzorgende IG mbo niveau 3.

Daarnaast:

  • Wil je invloed hebben op het invullen van je eigen diensten en werktijden;

  • Vind je het leuk om op verschillende locaties en met verschillende doelgroepen te werken;

  • Ben je flexibel inzetbaar, ook in de avonden, weekenden en op feestdagen;

  • Heb je voldoende digitale vaardigheden om goed met een computer en smartphone te kunnen werken.

Hebben wij jouw interesse kunnen wekken?

Solliciteer direct op de vacature via de knop ‘reageren’.

Wil je liever eerst even telefonisch contact, neem dan contact op met het flexpunt regio Uden 06-16830415.

title: Moderators - Health and Social Care
description:
Overview

Flexible Worker Contract

Location: Remote

About the role

We're looking for Moderators to join our External Quality Assurance team on a flexible worker contract for the following qualification:

Level 1/2 Technical Award in Health and Social Care

As a Moderator, you'll play a key role in ensuring that centres assess learners fairly, accurately and consistently. You'll review centre-marked work, apply quality assurance principles, and provide clear, constructive feedback to ensure national standards are maintained.

We’re keen to hear from individuals with a strong background in health and social care, with experience of teaching and/or assessing learners in this subject area. You may currently work, or have previously worked, as a Health and Social Care Teacher, Health and Social Care Lecturer or Health and Social Care Assessor.

Whilst this is a flexible worker role, we require a reasonable level of commitment throughout the moderation window. Moderation activities begin in March 2027 where you will be expected to attend one of our Annual Training sessions. The primary moderation period will be between April and August 2027, during which your engagement will be most critical.

How you’ll make an impact:

  • Conducting moderation activities in line with awarding organisation and regulatory requirements
  • Attending standardisation and team meetings as required
  • Reviewing centre marking to ensure assessment decisions are accurate, consistent and meet required standards
  • Producing clear, accurate and timely moderation reports within agreed Service Level Agreements (SLAs)
  • Planning and managing moderation activity for allocated centres in line with sampling strategies and quality assurance requirements
  • Supporting continuous improvement by identifying areas for development and sharing best practice
  • Maintaining up-to-date knowledge of the qualification, assessment requirements and your subject-specialist area

We'd love to hear from you if you offer the following:

  • A relevant qualification at Level 3 or above in health and social care or a closely related subject area
  • Current or recent occupational experience working within the health and social sector
  • Experience of teaching, assessing, internal quality assuring and/or moderating vocational or academic qualifications
  • Strong knowledge of assessment and quality assurance processes
  • Excellent written communication and report-writing skills
  • Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to work independently and meet deadlines
  • A commitment to maintaining high standards and delivering a positive experience for centres

Feeling inspired? Read the full Job Description

Our flexible workforce provides supportive quality assurance to ensure that learners taking NCFE qualifications are getting the best education possible. If you become a flexible worker with us, you’ll choose how to fit your work around your other personal and professional commitments – making this a great opportunity to make a difference in a way that suits you.

You’ll receive full training and the materials, tools or equipment needed to ensure you’re able to complete your duties in line with NCFE requirements, with the ability to take on flexible worker contract alongside other work, without the need to be registered as self-employed.

All applicants will be expected to adhere to NCFE’s behavioural framework and to uphold our core values.

You can find out more about how our flexible arrangements work, the flexible worker roles we recruit, and frequently asked questions around the application, induction and training process, and your rights and protections by visiting our Flexible worker opportunities page.

Shape real change with an NCFE career

Imagine a career where your contributions affect not only what people learn, but the way that learning is developed and delivered.

With over 170 years of education experience our core purpose remains at the heart of the organisation – to promote and advance learning to create a fairer, more inclusive society, making sure no learner is left behind.

Want to know more? Take a look at our website https://www.ncfe.org.uk/

How to apply

Before applying, please note that we require all candidates to be able to demonstrate proof of Right to Work in the UK.

Ready to join us and shape real change? Apply with your CV and answer the associated application questions.

Closing Date: Wednesday 2 December 2026

Interview Date: Ongoing

Interview Details: Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. If your application is shortlisted, we’ll contact you to complete a short task.

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) statement

We're committed to building rich diversity into our workforce at all levels, to ensure that we understand and are representative of the communities and customers we serve.

We do not discriminate against anyone due to their gender, sexuality, race, age, religion, beliefs, identity, social background, visible or hidden disability, or neurodiversity. Instead, we pride ourselves on our collaborative, vibrant and high-performance culture which embraces everyone, celebrates uniqueness, and enables everyone's voice to be heard.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description:
Part 2

  • Tech Lab

Senior DevOps Engineer

Build a company's entire delivery platform from the first commit, own it outright, and never carry a pager. Both halves of that sentence are deliberate.

  • Barcelona
  • on site
  • Open
  • 1 seat

What you own

  • 01 Infrastructure-as-code, from zero
  • 02 CI/CD and the release path
  • 03 Secrets management, including for agents
  • 04 Observability, backup and a tested restore

In Your First Few Months You Will

  • Build the platform from code. Hosts, networking, ingress, access, environments — committed, parameterised, reviewable. It is the cheapest moment this will ever be done, and you get to do it properly instead of retrofitting it.
  • Make deployment self-serve. Today, shipping an existing app is a git push; standing up a new one needs admin rights and two undocumented footguns. That gap is yours to close, down to one command, so a developer never holds a platform credential.
  • Own secrets properly. A real machine secrets manager, and — because we run a lot of AI agents — credentials brokered so an agent process only ever holds a placeholder, never a key. If you have opinions about how you stop a prompt-injected agent leaking a production credential, you will enjoy this part; almost nobody gets to design it from scratch.
  • Prove the restore. We have a written standard that says "someone deploys it" is not "someone has proven the restore works." You will run the drill and write the report.
  • Build the release path. Commit to production, an automated test gate, per-branch preview URLs a stakeholder can open from their phone, and a rollback that everyone on the team has rehearsed before they need it.
  • Then keep it all running — and keep making it duller. Observability, cost caps, dependency hygiene, the unglamorous work that decides whether a small team can own a lot of products.
And you will have the authority to match.

You are not inheriting a platform. You are writing one.

There is no infrastructure-as-code in our estate today — not a line. Your first job is to make that permanently untrue: every environment we run reproducible from a committed repo, from your first week, before the habit sets.

No rota, no pager, no phone number, no "just keep an eye on it this weekend". We are telling you this up front because it is not a perk we are quietly hoping you will waive.

Here is the honest other half, and it is the actual job:

We can only make that promise because we protect ourselves with engineering instead of with people's evenings — and that engineering is what we are hiring you to build. Infrastructure as code, so a lost machine is rebuilt rather than resurrected. Backups with a restore we have actually tested. A rollback that is one click and that everyone has already practised. Alerting that queues instead of paging, because nothing on the other end of it is expected to answer at night.

So the trade is explicit:

You are never woken up, and in exchange the systems have to be genuinely recoverable. If you have spent a career being paged for things that should have been engineered away, this is the version of the job where you get to do the engineering instead.

During working hours it is the opposite of hands-off.

The PO, the developers and the DevOps engineer assigned to a product own that product's incidents — support is not shipped off to a separate team, it is part of owning the thing, and it is what keeps everyone honest about quality.

How we build — deliberately boring, and you get a say in it

We have a settled stack and it is the same in most repos on purpose: one scaffold, shared packages, push-to-deploy. The payoff is that a two-person team can pick up a product they have never seen and be useful the same day, which is the only reason a team this size can own this many products.

We build the simplest platform that meets the requirement, and we are strict about what the requirement actually is.

Complexity here has to earn its place: every capability we run is one more thing one team has to understand, patch and be able to rebuild.

A concrete example, because it tells you a lot about us: we do not run Kubernetes, and that was a decision rather than an omission.

We looked at it properly, twice — most recently because we were worried we had got it wrong — and both times the answer was that a small portfolio on predictable traffic does not need multi-node scheduling and autoscaling badly enough to pay for them with the only infrastructure engineer we have. We wrote down the specific conditions under which we would change our minds, and when one of them is met, we will.

Which is why we are asking for someone who has run Kubernetes in production and can tell us when it is not the answer.

If your idea of a good week is tuning a cluster, this is the wrong job and we would rather you knew now. If your idea of a good platform is one a small team can fully understand, rebuild from a repo and hand to a new joiner in an afternoon — and you have enough scar tissue to know where that stops being enough — that judgement is most of what we are hiring.

It is a default, not a straitjacket.

Some things genuinely need something else, and when they do we adapt deliberately, with the reasoning written down. What we do not do is re-decide the same five questions on every new repo out of habit.

And you get a say in what the standard is.

Anyone can propose a change — something new that is genuinely better, something we should upgrade to, something we got wrong. A proposal gets researched properly against the alternatives, it gets an answer, and if the answer is no you get the reasoning. On infrastructure, you are not one voice among many — you are the one who decides, within a budget you help set.

You will get seriously good at building with AI agents

We are an AI-native engineering team, genuinely — not a team that added a Copilot licence. Every engineer gets their own Claude Max subscription and a desktop orchestrator that runs several coding agents in parallel, each in its own branch. That is true of you too: a great deal of infrastructure work is now specified rather than typed, and you will get very good at driving that — where it works, where it fails, and how to read a diff and decide whether it is actually right.

It Also Makes Your Job More Interesting Than The Same Title Elsewhere, Because Agentic Engineering Creates Infrastructure Problems Most Teams Do Not Have Yet

  • Agents install packages into code that sits next to client data. Supply-chain hygiene stops being a compliance checkbox and becomes a live control you own.
  • Agents hold credentials — or rather, they must not. Brokering machine identity so the agent never touches the real key is a design problem, and it is yours.
  • Agents cost money in a way that is invisible until the invoice. Per-project budgets, hard caps and an alert that fires before the cap, not after it.
  • Agents can deploy. Which means the guardrails between "an agent proposed this" and "this is in production" are infrastructure, not policy.

If you have been running agents seriously and have opinions about where they break, we want to hear them. If you are curious but not yet deep in it, that is fine — teaching this well is something we intend to be known for.

Things worth knowing up front

  • This is an on-site role in Barcelona. More than the other seats here, and for a real reason: you are standing up physical-ish infrastructure and access for a team being assembled around you, in its first year, and most of that goes faster in a room.
  • You are the only DevOps engineer for a while. That is authority, and it is also a bus factor — which is why "nothing exists only in one person's head" is written into the role rather than hoped for. Everything you build gets documented and reproducible as you go, not afterwards.

If you would be moving to Barcelona for this

  • We pay to get you here. Flights, your first month's accommodation while you find somewhere of your own, the visa and paperwork costs, and an agent to handle the bureaucracy — the NIE, the TIE appointment, the apostilles — instead of leaving you to meet the administrative system alone. Spanish lessons if you want them.
  • A relocation bonus, paid on arrival rather than dripped out. It is repayable only if you leave within the first eighteen months, and that condition is the reason we can pay it up front — moving countries costs money at the start, not in year two.

Three things here are worth more than they look on an offer comparison, particularly against a US one:

  • Nobody is on call. Ever. It has its own section above and we mean it literally. If you are coming from a market where infrastructure work and a pager are assumed to travel together, read that section twice — it is the single largest difference between this job and the same title elsewhere, and it is not a perk we are quietly hoping you will waive.
  • Healthcare with no premium, no deductible and no network — from day one, and not tied to staying in this job.
  • Thirty calendar days of holiday — that is 22 working days — plus fourteen public holidays, roughly seven weeks in total. That is the statutory floor in Spain, not a benefit we are being generous with.

And the on-site line reads differently depending on where you are standing. For someone already in Barcelona it is a constraint and we have said why. For someone moving here it is most of the point: this is a job in Barcelona, not a job you do from Barcelona — a team that sits together, in a city worth being physically present in.

What we are looking for

Read this as a description of the engineer you will be here, not a checklist you have to arrive with. Almost nobody ticks all of it on day one, and we would rather hire someone with the instinct and train the rest — that is a large part of what the certificate is for.

  • You have built infrastructure from nothing before, and it survived other people using it. A platform you were handed and maintained is fine; a platform you created is what we are asking for. This is the one non-negotiable, and it is why the role is senior: there is nobody here to check your work, and the platform you put in place is the one everyone else builds on for years.
  • Infrastructure-as-code is how you work, not a tool you have used. You can talk about what you do when reality and the repo disagree, because it always eventually does.
  • You have owned backups and actually restored from them — under time pressure, ideally when it mattered. Everyone has backups. Far fewer have restored.
  • You are comfortable running things on your own servers, not only on a managed cloud console. We own our infrastructure deliberately, and that is a different skill from configuring somebody else's.
  • You have run Kubernetes in production — and you are equally comfortable saying when it is not the right answer. We do not run it today. Whether and when we do is one of the decisions this job owns, and we would rather that call were made by someone who has lived with the thing than by someone reasoning about it from the outside.
  • You automate yourself out of the loop, and you write things down. The measure of this job is how little of it requires you specifically.
  • You can say no to complexity. The best engineer for this seat is the one who builds the boring thing that works and resists the interesting thing that does not need to exist.
  • Security is instinct, not a stage. Secrets, access, least privilege, patching — the boring disciplines, held consistently.
  • English, fluently. It is our working language — we work across roughly fifteen countries. Spanish is genuinely useful day to day. Catalan is not required.
  • Barcelona. This is a team that sits together, especially in its first year.
We do not care what you studied.

We care what you have built and run, and whether you can talk us through the decisions in it.

How we hire — the two rounds built for this seat

  • A thirty-minute conversation. What you have built, how you work, and how you think about it. We will ask you to walk us through something you built and then to justify a specific decision inside it. There is no way to prepare for that and it is not meant to catch you out; it is how we tell understanding from familiarity.
  • A project. We give you a brief and a working environment to build it in, with Claude Code already set up and wired to a key, so you are building the way we actually build rather than talking about it at a whiteboard. It is real work, not a puzzle, you do it on your own schedule — no week off, no flights, nothing that requires you to already be free — and we go through what you built together afterwards.

Mainloop

  • Barcelona.

title: Loss Prevention Expert, WWOS

To keep our operations network secure and assure operational continuity, we are looking for a proactive and solution-based professional who wants to join our team as Security and Loss Prevention (SLP) Expert. In this key role, you will deliver security as a service to our operational sites across the end-to-end supply chain to protect our people and prevent loss.

Key job responsibilities
• Support resilience of our business operations by contributing to emergency and crisis planning for sites within your area of responsibility
• Contribute to the identification of vulnerabilities (e.g., loss, associate experience, process improvement) and define appropriate mitigating actions while ensuring compliance with legal and ethical standards

• Ensure compliance of your assigned sites with Amazon global security standards
• Own Security and Loss Prevention-related projects on the local, regional, and country level


A day in the life
As an SLP Expert, you will join a team of Security and Loss Prevention professionals providing security as a service to business customers across multiple business units within a dedicated geographical area. You perform regular physical security audits and investigate policy violations, security-related incidents, and loss events. During your investigations, you collect information by monitoring systems and tools, analysing data reports, and conducting interviews.

Your findings contribute to identifying vulnerabilities in our processes and you identify and drive mitigating measures. You play a key role in maintaining the physical integrity of our sites by auditing and monitoring the health status of our systems and, jointly with subject matter experts and external suppliers, maintain their functionality. Furthermore, you identify and act upon initiatives improving our physical security infrastructure and contribute directly to the budgetary planning for our external suppliers.

You interact on a daily basis with our external security service providers to ensure delivery of high-quality security services and a smooth customer experience. Finally, you deliver loss prevention-related education and awareness programs to other teams across all management levels and manage the implementation of our Security and Loss Prevention plan.

About the team
Sitting within the Global Security Operations organisation, Security and Loss Prevention supports the accomplishment of Amazon´s business targets and the strengthening of our brand by effectively protecting against relevant threats and by managing security and loss prevention risks that could:

• Put our associates and customers under jeopardy
• Disrupt the continuity of our business operations
• Inflict damage to our assets
• Have adverse impact on our brand reputation

Working in partnership with our stakeholders, we secure the Amazon supply chain end-to-end and promote security during business conversations. We do this by preventing security and loss prevention-related risks and vulnerabilities as early as possible, intervening in unfolding incidents to minimize any negative impact as well as thoroughly investigating security-related incidents to identify and remove root causes, preventing re-occurrence.

Our DC Project Managers design, develop and deploy innovative solutions to address operational challenges. They work independently as well as the ability to work within multi-disciplinary teams. The Project Manager is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, implementation, execution, control and completion of specific projects ensuring consistency with company strategy, commitments and goals.

If you are passionate about the Customer Experience; you think big; and you want to contribute to the operational excellence of Amazon data centers then this may be the challenge you’ve been looking for!

- Recording and reporting key metrics to team members and management.

- Work with contractors and vendors to deliver efficient and high quality project turnovers.
- Be a leader within the group as well as within internal and external teams that support the data center.


A day in the life
You will be part of a highly creative, efficient team tasked with tackling the most fascinating and challenges in designing, building, and operating Amazon data facilities. The Project Manager is ultimately responsible for project oversight and review of all disciplines including electrical, mechanical, controls, and architectural. A fundamental understanding of these systems is required, you will be expected to identify areas for improvement as well as act on data provided from other team and organizations. Ideal candidates will possess the ability to design, develop and deploy innovative solutions to address operational challenges. This role requires both independent contribution as well as the ability to work within multi-disciplinary teams. The scope of projects will include but not limited to the improvement of electrical, mechanical, fire detection and building automation system. The Project Manager is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, implementation, execution, control and completion of specific projects ensuring consistency with company strategy, commitments and goals.

If you are passionate about the Customer Experience; you think big; and you want to contribute to the operational excellence of Amazon data centers then this may be the opportunity you’ve been looking for!

About the team

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. The Associate Director, AI Program Office serves as the single accountable leader bridging software engineering, product operations, enterprise productivity, and regulatory compliance.

Operating within the Office of the CTO, you will direct the AI Program Office across all major dimensions of enterprise AI utilization from software engineering acceleration and workforce productivity to autonomous operations and domain-specific applications. In our regulated healthcare and medical imaging environment, you will institute the operational standards, policies, and technical controls necessary to ensure that AI adoption remains safe, compliant, cost-effective, and directly aligned with measurable business value.

Enterprise AI Governance, Policy & Technical Controls

  • Architect, operationalize, and maintain the enterprise AI governance framework, establishing transparent decision gates, review workflows, and escalation pathways.

  • Author and maintain the enterprise AI Acceptable Use Policy, supported by SOPs, data-handling guardrails, and role-based permissions.

  • Translate policy into automated technical guardrails via API gateways, connector permissions, model endpoint access rules, and usage quotas.

  • Monitor emerging frameworks and legal mandates (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act, HIPAA, FDA SaMD guidance) and adapt internal compliance controls accordingly.

Tool Sanctioning & Central Registry

  • Own and curate the registry of sanctioned AI models, platforms, and API connectors across the organization.

  • Manage intake and multi-stakeholder evaluation of newly requested AI tools and capabilities.

  • Proactively identify, monitor, and mitigate unsanctioned “shadow AI” tools and integrations in partnership with Information Security.

  • Maintain onboarding standards so approved tools move from request to production quickly and safely.

Risk Review, Safety & Assurance

  • Run a structured risk-assessment intake for emerging AI use cases, internal prompts/fine-tunes, and third-party AI integrations.

  • Maintain complete governance artifacts, including algorithmic impact assessments, model cards, audit logs, and exception approvals.

  • Partner closely with:

    • Information Security

    • Legal

    • Privacy

    • Quality/Regulatory Affairs

  • Validate control effectiveness, address audit findings, and support customer and regulatory inquiries.

AI FinOps, Token Budgets & Cost Optimization

  • Define usage thresholds, token allocation quotas, and department-level spend caps across enterprise AI models and platforms.

  • Build and oversee enterprise AI visibility reporting to monitor usage patterns, token efficiency, license utilization, and latency metrics.

  • Design and operate an equitable cross-business-unit chargeback and showback mechanism, identifying consolidation and volume-discount opportunities.

Program Roadmap & Use Case Factory

  • Spearhead enterprise-wide adoption programs for core foundational platforms and emerging cognitive tools.

  • Prioritize use-case intake across clinical operations, corporate functions, and engineering to maintain a high-ROI implementation backlog.

  • Define KPIs and measure quantifiable outcomes, reporting program health directly to the CTO and executive leadership.

Strategic Vendor & Partner Management

  • Act as the primary relationship owner for technology partners, and emerging AI vendors.

  • Negotiate enterprise agreements, data confidentiality addenda (BAAs, zero-data-retention terms), license tiers, and performance SLAs in coordination with Procurement and Legal.

  • Manage contract renewals and performance reviews to ensure ongoing value and compliance.

Enablement, Training & AI Culture

  • Drive enterprise AI fluency through tailored role-based curricula, prompt-engineering playbooks, and interactive office hours.

  • Serve as an internal consultant for department heads and product teams, turning ambitious business ideas into practical, compliant AI implementations.

  • Promote a culture of responsible AI adoption in partnership with change management and communications teams.

PLEASE NOTE: This is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and requirements of the position described above. Other functions may be assigned and management retains the right to add or change duties at any time.

Minimum Qualifications, Education and Experience

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Health Informatics, Information Systems, Business Administration, or a related field (Master’s or MBA preferred).

  • 8+ years of progressive leadership in technology program management, technology strategy, enterprise architecture, or IT risk/compliance, including 3+ years driving enterprise-wide technical transformation programs.

  • Proven track record operationalizing technology, data, or AI governance programs within regulated environments (Healthcare, Life Sciences, MedTech, or Financial Services).

  • Deep understanding of modern generative AI, agentic frameworks, LLM architectures, and associated risks (data leakage, IP exposure, bias, hallucination, non-deterministic behaviors).

  • Familiarity with API gateways, identity and access management (IAM), data loss prevention (DLP), and cloud network access policies.

  • Exceptional communication skills with demonstrated success aligning cross-functional executives across Engineering, Clinical Operations, Legal, Compliance, and Finance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct background in digital health, radiology/medical imaging, or medical software environments subject to FDA (SaMD), HIPAA, SOC 2, or GxP regulations.

  • Hands-on experience establishing AI FinOps, token consumption governance, or showback/chargeback models across multiple subsidiaries or business units.

  • Relevant certifications such as IAPP Certified Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional (AIGP), CIPP, CISM, PMP, or SAFe Agilist.

  • Direct experience negotiating enterprise AI software agreements and vendor terms.

Quality Standards

  • Communicates, cooperates, and consistently functions professionally and harmoniously with all levels of supervision, co-workers, visitors, and vendors.

  • Demonstrates initiative, personal awareness, professionalism and integrity, and exercises confidentiality in all areas of performance.

  • Follows all local, regional and country laws concerning employment.

  • Follows all DeepHealth policies and procedures.

  • Follows data privacy, compliance, safety and confidentiality standards at all times.

  • Practices universal safety precautions.

  • Promotes good public relations on the phone and in person.

  • Adapts and is willing to learn new tasks, methods, and systems.

  • Reports to work regularly as scheduled; consistently punctual with respect to working hours, meal and rest breaks, and maintains satisfactory personal attendance in accordance with DeepHealth guidelines.

  • Completes job responsibilities in a quality and timely manner.

Travel

This position requires domestic/international travel up to 15%.

Working Environment

Remote / Hybrid

title: Pedagogisch Begeleider | Vesper BSO
description:
Bij Vesper kijken we naar wat wél kan. Wij zijn een BSO voor kinderen met een extra ondersteuningsbehoefte, bijvoorbeeld door autisme, ADHD of een (licht) verstandelijke beperking. En we groeien! Daarom zoeken we op meerdere locaties in de Randstad pedagogisch begeleiders.

Functieomschrijving

Vesper groeit en daarom zijn we op zoek naar een extra collega! Daarvoor zijn we op zoek naar een Pedagogisch Begeleider met ervaring op het gebied van gedrags- en/of ontwikkelingsproblematiek.


Als Pedagogisch Begeleider zet je op de groep een veilig klimaat neer waar leren, spelen en ontspannen centraal staat. Dit zijn de drie (belangrijkste) pijlers bij Vesper die we de kinderen bieden. Samen met een collega draai je een groep van 8 tot 10 kinderen die in kleine groepjes of juist alleen spelen. Je begeleidt de kinderen en zorgt voor structuur, duidelijkheid en positieve bekrachtiging in de keuzes die de kinderen maken.


In een gestructureerde en veilige omgeving krijgen de kinderen de ruimte om te (leren) ontspannen, te spelen en te oefenen aan een stukje zelfstandigheid en sociaal contact.


Als Pedagogisch Begeleider bedenk je activiteiten waarmee kinderen aangeleerde vaardigheden oefenen, in de praktijk en in het contact met andere kinderen. Hierbij kun je denken aan situaties die de sociale vaardigheden vergroten van een 10-jarige jongen met autisme of die het zelfbeeld versterken van een angstig meisje van 7 jaar. Kennis en ervaring met de doelgroep, kinderen met een ontwikkelingsstoornis zoals autisme of ADHD, is dus onmisbaar.

Functie-eisen

Je bent een echte doener met een groot hart voor kinderen. Initiatief nemen en zelfstandig werken geeft jou veel energie. Het is jouw missie om de kinderen een fijne BSO-middag te bieden waarin je zowel voor structuur en geborgenheid zorgt, als een leuke activiteit. Je kunt goed communiceren en samenwerken. Een must wanneer je met onze kinderen werkt. Vesper is een snel groeiende organisatie met de missie om zoveel mogelijk opvang te bieden aan kinderen met een extra ondersteuningsbehoefte. Jij kunt niet wachten om hier samen met ons je schouders onder te zetten!

Je beschikt over de volgende kwalificaties:

  • Je hebt een afgeronde Mbo- of Hbo-opleiding in de richting van pedagogiek (SPW 3 of 4, onderwijsassistent, Hbo pedagogiek, toegepaste psychologie met uitstroomprofiel jeugd/onderwijs, sport en beweging met uitstroomprofiel jeugd/onderwijs)

  • Je hebt bij voorkeur ervaring met het begeleiden van kinderen in onze doelgroep, of hebt ervaring als pedagogisch medewerker in de kinderopvang en wil je graag specialiseren.

  • Je bent een enthousiast, sociaal en gedreven persoon die een proactieve en zelfstandige werkhouding heeft;

  • Je bent op zoek naar een uitdaging voor op de lange termijn!

Aanvullende informatie

Vesper biedt je niet alleen een ontzettend leuke en dynamische werkomgeving, we hechten veel waarde aan jouw talent en persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Eigen initiatief en inbreng wordt zeer gewaardeerd, verras ons met jouw ideeën! Daarnaast biedt Vesper jou als Pedagogisch Begeleider:

  • Een jaarcontract tussen de 18 en 32 uur per week, met uitzicht op vast contract.

  • Een bruto maandsalaris tussen de € 2.681,- tot € 3.684, - per maand (schaal 6 CAO Kinderopvang) op basis van een 36-urige werkweek;

  • 8% vakantiegeld en een eindejaarsuitkering van 8%;

  • 210 vakantie- en verlofuren op jaarbasis, maar alleen als je belooft dat je terugkomt (op basis van een 36-urige werkweek);

  • Een vergoeding van je reiskosten;

  • Diverse mogelijkheden om jezelf verder te ontwikkelen als specialist!

Translate high-level needs into clear functional/technical specifications (User Stories, Acceptance Criteria, and Process Maps) while managing and prioritizing the product backlog against the MVP.

What are we looking for?

  • Agile Product Management: Advanced expertise in Agile methodologies, including backlog refinement, sprint management, and strict prioritization of features to ensure the delivery of the Minimum Viable Product (MVP).
  • Testing & Quality Engineering: Deep knowledge of the testing lifecycle, specifically in designing complex Integration System Testing (IST) for APIs/interfaces and leading User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Experienced in defect management and ensuring full traceability from requirement to test case.
  • Systems & Data Integration Analysis: Strong understanding of application architecture, system interfaces, data flows, and integration patterns (e.g., APIs, Data Virtualization). Ability to analyze data quality and ensure consistency across multiple REFERENTIALS data sources.
  • Software & Tooling Mastery: Proficiency in ALM Octane (for requirement-to-test traceability and defect management), Jira (for task/backlog tracking), and Confluence (for documentation and collaboration).

  • Social events and team buildings;
  • The commitment of letting you grow with us, and be rewarded accordingly;
